title: API Token Controls
scope: Admin controls, logging and revocation for API credentials on SaaS platforms. Sourced from vendor documentation; not an audit of any tenant.

definitions.conditional: Documented, with plan, policy or endpoint conditions.
definitions.excluded: The named control explicitly does not cover this credential.
definitions.not_supported: Vendor documentation states this credential lacks the control.
definitions.unknown: No source found either way. Not a negative finding.
definitions.not_verified: No source found either way. Not a negative finding.
definitions.not_applicable: Does not apply to this credential.
definitions.limited: Documented for a narrower case only.

providers.name: Databricks (AWS baseline)
providers.scope_notes: AWS IP-access-list docs require Enterprise tier. Azure/GCP capabilities and licensing must be checked separately.

controls.name: IP access lists
controls.what: Restrict account console/account APIs and workspace/workspace APIs to approved IPs.
controls.setting: Account console IP access lists; workspace IP Access List API
controls.quote: The default allows connections from any IP address.

controls.name: Context-based ingress policies
controls.what: Account-level allow/deny rules combining identity, network source and request scope, e.g. pinning service principals to trusted networks.
controls.quote: allow and deny rules that combine who is calling, from where they are calling, and what they can reach

controls.name: Service principal federation policy
controls.what: Binds a service principal to tokens from a given issuer, audience and subject.
controls.setting: Account console > service principal > Credentials & secrets; Federation Policy API/CLI (account admin)
controls.quote: Account admins can configure a service principal federation policy

controls.name: Account-wide federation policy
controls.what: Allows tokens from a registered IdP to map to Databricks users or service principals; only trusted IdPs should be added.
controls.setting: Account console > Security > federation policy; Account Federation Policy API
controls.quote: Don't configure account-wide federation with external IdPs that you don't control.

controls.name: Deactivate a service principal
controls.what: Deactivated service principals cannot authenticate; their OAuth secrets and tokens stop working until reactivated.
controls.setting: Account Service Principals API (account level); Workspace Service Principals API (workspace level)

controls_unknown: No account-wide switch to disable PATs across all workspaces was found; the toggle is per workspace.
Whether IP access lists explicitly cover PAT/OAuth API calls is implied (workspace-level APIs) but not stated.
Whether context-based ingress rules can distinguish auth method (PAT vs OAuth) is not stated.
How to update or delete federation policies, and how to revoke an individual OAuth secret, were not covered on the fetched pages.
TTL min/max ranges, and whether built-in databricks-cli app follows app-connection TTL defaults, not confirmed.
Single-use refresh token details page returned 404; defaults per app not confirmed.
Azure/GCP capabilities and tiers not checked.

authentication.summary: OAuth user-to-machine and machine-to-machine, external token federation, and legacy personal access tokens.

federation.details: External IdP tokens exchange into Databricks OAuth using configured issuer/audience/subject trust; workload CI/runtime federation supported.

ip_restriction.boundary: Enterprise tier. Separate account/workspace IP lists protect public UI/API access; PrivateLink traffic is not filtered by them. Context-based ingress (Enterprise) can add rules combining identity (e.g. service principal), network source and access type.

renewal.summary: Repeat token exchange using a valid external identity token.

administration.summary: Service principals, entitlements/resource ACLs, federation policies, PAT controls and context-based ingress controls.
administration.conditions: AWS IP-access-list docs require Enterprise tier. Azure/GCP capabilities and licensing must be checked separately.

sso.details: Tokens are issued by your own IdP, so its policies apply at issuance; Databricks does not describe SSO checks on the exchanged token.

offboard.details: A deactivated user or service principal cannot authenticate to Databricks APIs; SCIM removal deactivates the user.

sso.ui: Account console > Security > Identity provider setup > Federation policies > Create policy (issuer, audiences, subject); per SP: User management > <SP> > Credentials & secrets > Federation policies

expiry.ui: Set in your IdP: Databricks token copies the subject token exp claim

reads.api: SQL: SELECT * FROM system.access.audit WHERE service_name='workspace' AND action_name='workspaceExport' (filter user_identity.email)

offboard.ui: Remove the user from the IdP account-level SCIM connector (deactivates the user)

token_format.notes: Input is an external IdP JWT (RS256/ES256); output is a Databricks OAuth token whose exp equals the JWT exp. GitHub type databricks_federated_account_session_token exists.

log_sources.name: Databricks audit logs (system.access.audit system table / audit log delivery)
log_sources.notes: Account- and workspace-level events; account-level rows have workspace_id 0. No general retention stated on the table page; events of a deleted workspace older than 14 days are removed.

log_sources.name: External IdP / workload identity provider logs
log_sources.notes: Issuance of the federated JWT happens at the IdP; Databricks logs only the exchange and use.

credential_id_fields.notes: Present for service principal (workload identity) policies
Service principal UUID for workload identity federation exchanges
Databricks identity the federated token maps to

lifecycle_events.notes: Account-wide or SP federation policy created
Token minted; grant_type would be the token-exchange URN
API call authorized with OAuth token

anomaly_cues: createFederationPolicy or updateFederationPolicy adding an unfamiliar issuer or broad audience
policy change by an admin outside change windows followed by token-exchange mints
token-exchange mintOAuthToken from IPs not belonging to the CI/cloud workload
account-wide policy subject_claim changed (could let one IdP user map to another Databricks user)
federated tokens used after IdP-side workload was decommissioned

containment.steps: Delete or tighten the federation policy (deleteFederationPolicy); deactivate the mapped service principal or user; revoke/rotate trust at the external IdP.
containment.notes: Docs do not state whether deleting a policy invalidates already-exchanged Databricks tokens; those expire at the JWT exp (commonly one hour). SP deactivation blocks its tokens.

sample_query.query: SELECT event_time, action_name, user_identity.email, request_params['policy_id'] AS policy_id, request_params['service_principal_id'] AS sp_id, source_ip_address FROM system.access.audit WHERE service_name = 'accounts' AND action_name IN ('createFederationPolicy','updateFederationPolicy','deleteFederationPolicy') ORDER BY event_time DESC
sample_query.purpose: Review who changed federation trust and for which service principal

unknown: whether mintOAuthToken is logged for token-exchange grants (only documented as in-house OAuth token minted)
policy issuer/audience values in audit request_params
external JWT subject/issuer in Databricks audit rows
effect of policy deletion on issued tokens

calls.reveals: Notebook or whole-directory contents (source code, sometimes embedded secrets/results)
calls.log_notes: Audit log / system.access.audit; user_identity shows the caller. Docs describe the event as a notebook export.
